words.gloss: with grain, men and supplies cut off

hindi: सेना के व्यसन ये हैं — असम्मानित, अपमानित, अवैतनिक, रोगग्रस्त, नई आई हुई, दूर से आई हुई, थकी हुई, क्षीण, पीछे हटाई गई, जिसके अग्रभाग का वेग नष्ट हो गया हो, अनुचित ऋतु में पहुँची हुई, अनुचित भूमि पर पहुँची हुई, आशा से निराश, भाग निकली हुई, भीतर स्त्रियों से भरी हुई, भीतर शल्य वाली, कुपित मूल वाली, टूटे हुए गर्भ वाली, पीछे हटी हुई, बहुत दूर फेंकी गई, डेरा डाले हुए, शत्रु से सटी हुई, घेरी गई, चारों ओर से घिरी हुई, जिसके धान्य, पुरुष और रसद कट गए हों, अपनी भूमि में बिखरी हुई, मित्र की भूमि में बिखरी हुई, दूष्यों से युक्त, दुष्ट पार्ष्णिग्राह वाली, शून्य मूल वाली, स्वामी के बिना इकट्ठी हुई, टूटे हुए कूट वाली और अन्धी — इति।
english: The calamities of the army: unhonoured, dishonoured, unpaid, sick, newly arrived, come from afar, exhausted, depleted, repulsed, with its front charge destroyed, arrived in the wrong season, arrived on unsuitable ground, despairing of its hopes, run away, encumbered with women within, with a thorn within, with a disaffected base, with a split core, withdrawn, driven too far, encamped, closely joined with the enemy, besieged, surrounded, with its grain, men and supplies cut off, scattered in its own territory, scattered in an ally's territory, joined with treasonable persons, with a dangerous heel-seizer, with an empty base, assembled without a master, with its chief broken off, and blind — thus.
notes: All thirty-three items are neuter nominative singular agreeing with balam (army). Each is explained in 8.5.2-18 below, which fixes the sense taken here: mūla = base (home territory/rear), garbha = core (interior of the army), kūṭa = chief/leader, andha = blind (without a guide, adeśika), samāpta = come into one place with the enemy, parisṛpta = run away (chiefs deserted), vīvadha = supplies brought from outside. sattra, pārṣṇi-grāha, dūṣya as in the glossary.

words.gloss: of the unhonoured and the dishonoured

hindi: इनमें असम्मानित और अपमानित के बीच, असम्मानित सेना धन और सम्मान पा लेने पर लड़ेगी, पर अपमानित सेना नहीं, जिसके भीतर क्रोध है।
english: Of these, between the unhonoured and the dishonoured, the unhonoured one would fight when it has been given wealth and honour, not the dishonoured one, which has anger within.

text_flags.why: possible: every other unit of the chapter pairs exactly the two listed items in a genitive dual (X.Yyoḥ); the extra member 'aniyata' is not in the list of 8.5.1 and is not taken up in the sentence; the split follows the two-member reading

notes: If 'aniyatayoḥ' is genuine the compound would have three members with a dual ending, which does not fit; the two-member reading is assumed.

words.gloss: of the unpaid and the sick
whose wages are paid at once

hindi: अवैतनिक और रोगग्रस्त के बीच, अवैतनिक सेना तुरन्त वेतन दिए जाने पर लड़ेगी, पर रोगग्रस्त सेना नहीं, जो काम के अयोग्य है।
english: Between the unpaid and the sick, the unpaid one would fight when its wages are paid on the spot, not the sick one, which is unfit for work.
notes: tadātva = the present moment; tadātva-kṛta-vetana = with pay given immediately.

words.gloss: of the newly arrived and the come-from-afar
with the fatigue of a long march

hindi: नई आई हुई और दूर से आई हुई के बीच, नई आई हुई सेना दूसरों से देश की जानकारी पाकर और पुराने सैनिकों के साथ मिलकर लड़ेगी, पर दूर से आई हुई सेना नहीं, जिसे लम्बी यात्रा की थकान है।
english: Between the newly arrived and the one come from afar, the newly arrived one would fight when it has learnt the terrain from others and is mixed with troops that are not new, not the one come from afar, which has the fatigue of a long march.

text_flags.why: possible: the list in 8.5.1 and the dual at the head of this unit read dūra.āyātam (past participle of ā-√yā); āyatam here looks like a dropped long vowel

notes: anyata = anyataḥ (visarga lost before u-). āyata-gata = having gone a long way; anava-miśra = mixed with troops that are not new (veterans).

words.gloss: of the exhausted and the depleted
having got rest by bathing, food and sleep
whose draught animals and men are lost

hindi: थकी हुई और क्षीण के बीच, थकी हुई सेना स्नान, भोजन और नींद से विश्राम पा लेने पर लड़ेगी, पर क्षीण सेना नहीं, जिसके वाहन-पशु और पुरुष किसी अन्य युद्ध में नष्ट हो चुके हैं।
english: Between the exhausted and the depleted, the exhausted one would fight when it has obtained rest through bathing, food and sleep, not the depleted one, whose draught animals and men have been lost in a battle elsewhere.
notes: yugya = draught/riding animals (yoked animals). The e-text writes kṣīṇayugya without the member dot; the split is kṣīṇa-yugya-puruṣa.

words.gloss: of the repulsed and the one whose front charge is destroyed
the one whose front charge is destroyed
whose heroes were killed in the first onset

hindi: पीछे हटाई गई और जिसके अग्रभाग का वेग नष्ट हो गया हो, इन दोनों के बीच, पहले आक्रमण में टूटी हुई पीछे हटाई गई सेना श्रेष्ठ वीर पुरुषों के साथ संगठित होकर लड़ेगी, पर वह सेना नहीं जिसके अग्रभाग का वेग नष्ट हो गया हो, जिसके वीर पहले आक्रमण में मारे जा चुके हैं।
english: Between the repulsed and the one whose front charge is destroyed, the repulsed one, broken in the first onset, would fight when rallied together with eminent brave men, not the one whose front charge is destroyed, whose heroes have been killed in the first onset.
notes: agra-pāta = the first clash/onset; agra-vega = the impetus of the vanguard.

words.gloss: of the one arrived in the wrong season and the one arrived on unsuitable ground
the one arrived in the wrong season
with animals, weapons and armour suited to the season
the one arrived on unsuitable ground
whose spreading out and movement are obstructed

hindi: अनुचित ऋतु में पहुँची हुई और अनुचित भूमि पर पहुँची हुई के बीच, अनुचित ऋतु में पहुँची हुई सेना ऋतु के अनुकूल वाहन-पशु, शस्त्र और कवच पाकर लड़ेगी, पर अनुचित भूमि पर पहुँची हुई सेना नहीं, जिसका फैलाव और गति रुकी हुई है।
english: Between the one arrived in the wrong season and the one arrived on unsuitable ground, the one arrived in the wrong season would fight when provided with draught animals, weapons and armour suited to the season, not the one arrived on unsuitable ground, whose spreading out and movement are obstructed.
notes: anṛtv.abhūmi = anṛtu + abhūmi with sandhi (u > v) shown in the e-text; yatha.ṛtu = yathā-ṛtu (yathartu), 'according to the season'.

words.gloss: of the one despairing of hope and the one run away
the one despairing of its hopes

hindi: आशा से निराश और भाग निकली हुई के बीच, आशा से निराश सेना अपनी इच्छा पूरी हो जाने पर लड़ेगी, पर भाग निकली हुई सेना नहीं, जिसके मुख्य पुरुष हट चुके हैं।
english: Between the one despairing of its hopes and the one that has run away, the one despairing of its hopes would fight when its wish has been fulfilled, not the one that has run away, whose chief men have deserted.

words.gloss: of the one encumbered with women and the one with a thorn within
the one encumbered with women within
the one with a thorn within

hindi: स्त्रियों से भरी हुई और भीतर शल्य वाली के बीच, स्त्रियों से भरी हुई सेना स्त्रियों को छोड़कर लड़ेगी, पर भीतर शल्य वाली सेना नहीं, जिसके भीतर शत्रु है।
english: Between the one encumbered with women and the one with a thorn within, the one encumbered with women would fight after leaving the women behind, not the one with a thorn within, which has an enemy within.
notes: antara.mitram: the e-text's member dot suggests antara-mitra, but the sense of the pair (explaining antaḥ-śalya, 'a thorn inside') requires antar-amitra, 'with an enemy inside'; the same letters are read that way here. kalatra = wives/family accompanying the army; garbhy. = garbhi + a- with sandhi.

words.gloss: of the one with a disaffected base and the one with a split core
the one with a disaffected base
the one with a split core

hindi: कुपित मूल वाली और टूटे हुए गर्भ वाली के बीच, कुपित मूल वाली सेना साम आदि उपायों से क्रोध शान्त किए जाने पर लड़ेगी, पर टूटे हुए गर्भ वाली सेना नहीं, जो आपस में एक-दूसरे से फूटी हुई है।
english: Between the one with a disaffected base and the one with a split core, the one with a disaffected base would fight when its anger has been pacified by conciliation and the other means, not the one with a split core, which is divided from one another.
notes: sāma-ādi = the four means beginning with conciliation (sāman, dāna, bheda, daṇḍa); only 'conciliation and the rest' is said.

words.gloss: of the withdrawn and the one driven too far
relying on a hiding-place and an ally

hindi: पीछे हटी हुई और बहुत दूर फेंकी गई के बीच, एक राज्य को पार कर गई पीछे हटी हुई सेना मन्त्र और व्यायाम के द्वारा गुप्त स्थान और मित्र का सहारा लेकर लड़ेगी, पर बहुत दूर फेंकी गई सेना नहीं, जो अनेक राज्यों को पार कर गई है, क्योंकि उसे अनेक बाधाएँ हैं।
english: Between the withdrawn and the one driven too far, the withdrawn one, which has passed beyond one kingdom, would fight relying on a hiding-place and an ally, by means of counsel and activity, not the one driven too far, which has passed beyond many kingdoms, because of its many obstructions.
notes: sattra = a concealed place/ambush position (as in 8.5.19 sattra-sthāna). bahv.ābādhatvāt = bahu + ābādhatvāt with sandhi (u > v).

words.gloss: of the encamped and the closely joined
whose marching and halting are separate
whose halting and marching are in one place

hindi: डेरा डाले हुए और शत्रु से सटी हुई के बीच, डेरा डाले हुए सेना, जिसकी यात्रा और पड़ाव शत्रु से अलग हैं, शत्रु को छलकर लड़ेगी, पर शत्रु से सटी हुई सेना नहीं, जिसका पड़ाव और यात्रा शत्रु के साथ एक ही स्थान पर है।
english: Between the encamped and the closely joined, the encamped one, whose marching and halting are separate, would fight after outwitting the enemy, not the closely joined one, whose halting and marching are in one place with the enemy.
notes: samāpta is taken, from the explanation given, as 'come together into one place with the enemy'. pṛthag.yāna = pṛthak-yāna with sandhi (k > g).

words.gloss: of the besieged and the surrounded

hindi: घेरी गई और चारों ओर से घिरी हुई के बीच, घेरी गई सेना दूसरी ओर से निकलकर घेरने वाले से लड़ेगी, पर चारों ओर से घिरी हुई सेना नहीं, जो सब ओर से रोकी हुई है।
english: Between the besieged and the surrounded, the besieged one would go out by another side and fight back against the besieger, not the surrounded one, which is blocked on all sides.

words.gloss: of the one with grain cut off and the one with men and supplies cut off
the one with grain cut off
feeding on moving and stationary things
the one with men and supplies cut off

hindi: जिसका धान्य कट गया हो और जिसके पुरुष और रसद कट गए हों, इन दोनों के बीच, जिसका धान्य कट गया हो वह सेना दूसरी जगह से धान्य लाकर, अथवा चर और अचर वस्तुओं का आहार करके लड़ेगी, पर जिसके पुरुष और रसद कट गए हों वह सेना नहीं, जिसे कोई सहायता नहीं पहुँचती।
english: Between the one whose grain is cut off and the one whose men and supplies are cut off, the one whose grain is cut off would fight after bringing grain from elsewhere, or living on food from moving and stationary things, not the one whose men and supplies are cut off, which has no reinforcement coming.
notes: The head compound is a dvandva of chinna-dhānya and chinna-puruṣa-vīvadha. vīvadha = supplies carried in from outside; jaṅgama-sthāvara = animals and plants (literally moving and non-moving things); abhisāra = troops/help coming to join.

words.gloss: of the one scattered in its own territory and the one scattered in an ally's
the one scattered in its own territory
the one scattered in an ally's territory
because of remoteness of place and time

hindi: अपनी भूमि में बिखरी हुई और मित्र की भूमि में बिखरी हुई के बीच, अपनी भूमि में बिखरी हुई सेना को, जो अपनी भूमि में बिखरी हुई है, आपत्ति में बुला लेना सम्भव है, पर मित्र की भूमि में बिखरी हुई सेना को नहीं, क्योंकि स्थान और समय दूर हैं।
english: Between the one scattered in its own territory and the one scattered in an ally's territory, the one scattered in its own territory, an army dispersed in its own land, can be called together in a calamity, not the one scattered in an ally's territory, because of the remoteness of place and time.
notes: This unit has no yudhyeta; the predicate is śakyam āvāhayitum (can be summoned).

words.gloss: of the one joined with the treasonable and the one with a dangerous heel-seizer
the one joined with the treasonable
the one with a dangerous heel-seizer
fearful of an attack from behind

hindi: दूष्यों से युक्त और दुष्ट पार्ष्णिग्राह वाली के बीच, दूष्यों से युक्त सेना विश्वस्त पुरुषों के अधीन रखी जाकर और दूष्यों को संगठित न होने देकर लड़ेगी, पर दुष्ट पार्ष्णिग्राह वाली सेना नहीं, जो पीठ पीछे से आघात से डरी हुई है।
english: Between the one joined with the treasonable and the one with a dangerous heel-seizer, the one joined with the treasonable would fight when placed under trusted men and kept from combining, not the one with a dangerous heel-seizer, which is fearful of an attack from behind.
notes: asaṃhatam: taken as 'not allowed to combine' (the treasonable elements kept apart); it could also mean the army kept dispersed.

words.gloss: of the one with an empty base and the one assembled without a master
the one with an empty base
having arranged protection for citizens and country-people
with the whole mass of forces
the one assembled without a master

hindi: शून्य मूल वाली और स्वामी के बिना इकट्ठी हुई के बीच, शून्य मूल वाली सेना नगरवासियों और जनपदवासियों की रक्षा का प्रबन्ध करके अपनी सारी शक्ति समेटकर लड़ेगी, पर स्वामी के बिना इकट्ठी हुई सेना नहीं, जो राजा और सेनापति से रहित है।
english: Between the one with an empty base and the one assembled without a master, the one with an empty base would fight with its whole massed strength after arranging protection for the citizens and the country-people, not the one assembled without a master, which lacks a king and a commander of the army.
notes: sandoha = the total gathering (of forces). paura = townsfolk, jānapada = country-people.

words.gloss: of the one with its chief broken off and the blind one
the one with its chief broken off

hindi: टूटे हुए कूट वाली और अन्धी के बीच, टूटे हुए कूट वाली सेना किसी दूसरे के अधीन रखी जाकर लड़ेगी, पर अन्धी सेना नहीं, जिसके पास मार्ग जानने वाला कोई नहीं है। इति।
english: Between the one with its chief broken off and the blind one, the one with its chief broken off would fight when placed under another leader, not the blind one, which has no guide. Thus.
notes: kūṭa = the head/chief of the army; adeśika = without a deśika, one who knows the country and shows the way. The e-text has an inner danda before the closing iti.

words.gloss: the remedy for an army's calamity

hindi: दोष का दूर करना, सेना की वृद्धि, गुप्त स्थान से शत्रु को छलना और प्रबल पक्ष के साथ सन्धि — यह सेना के व्यसन का उपाय है।
english: Removal of the defect, addition of troops, outwitting from a position of concealment, and peace with the stronger side: this is the remedy for a calamity of the army.
notes: uttara-pakṣa = the superior/stronger party; atisaṃhita (n.) = deceiving/outwitting. sādhanam is singular with four subjects.

words.gloss: at the weak points of the army

hindi: सदा सावधान रहकर वह व्यसन में अपनी सेना की शत्रुओं से रक्षा करे; सदा सावधान रहकर वह शत्रुओं की सेना के छिद्रों पर प्रहार करे।
english: Ever alert, he should protect his own army from enemies in a calamity; ever alert, he should strike at the weak points of the enemies' armies.
notes: randhra = hole, weak point. utthita = risen, i.e. active and vigilant.

hindi: जिस कारण से वह प्रकृतियों का व्यसन पा सकता है, उस कारण का वह आलस्य छोड़कर पहले ही प्रतीकार करे।
english: The cause from which he might incur a calamity of the constituent elements — that cause he should counteract beforehand, unwearied.
notes: yato nimittam: 'from which cause' (nimittam nominative in loose apposition with yataḥ) and then tan nimittam resumes it as object.

hindi: जिस मित्र पर स्वयं, या दूसरों के साथ मिलकर, या दूसरे के वश में होकर चढ़ाई की गई हो; जो असमर्थता से, लोभ से या प्रेम के कारण छोड़ दिया गया हो;
english: An ally that has been marched against by oneself, or jointly with others, or at another's bidding; one abandoned through incapacity, or through greed, or through affection;
notes: 22-27 form one sentence: a list of allies (mitram, n. acc./nom.) wronged in these ways, concluded in 27cd by 'is won with difficulty and, once won, soon becomes disaffected'. praṇaya = affection (for someone else) or familiarity; taken literally.

words.gram: m. loc. sg. pres. part. ātm. abhi-√yuj

hindi: जो मित्र, जब कोई उस पर आक्रमण कर रहा हो या युद्ध में, मुँह मोड़ लेने वाले के द्वारा बेच दिया गया हो; या द्वैधीभाव के द्वारा, या शत्रु के पास जाने वाले के द्वारा, या अन्यत्र से किसी दूसरे के पास जाने वाले के द्वारा;
english: one sold out, when someone is attacking it or in battle, by one who turns away from it; or through the dual policy, or by one who is about to go over to the enemy, or to another from elsewhere;
notes: abhiyuñjāne is taken as a locative absolute-like 'when (someone) is attacking'; it could also be 'to the attacker' (sold out to the one attacking). anyam anyataḥ: going to another ally from another quarter; the exact construction is terse.

hindi: जो अलग रहकर या साथ-साथ यात्रा में विश्वास के कारण छला गया हो; या भय, अवज्ञा या आलस्य के कारण व्यसन से नहीं छुड़ाया गया हो;
english: one outwitted through its trust, either separately or in a joint march; or not rescued from a calamity through fear, contempt or laziness;
notes: vyasanān = vyasanāt with sandhi before n-.

hindi: जो अपनी भूमियों से रोक दिया गया हो, या पास से भय के कारण चला गया हो; जो छीन लेने से, न देने से, या देकर भी अपमानित किया गया हो;
english: one shut out from its own lands, or gone away from nearby through fear; one insulted by having things taken away, by not being given, or even after being given;
notes: samīpād gatam: 'gone away from his vicinity' (through fear of him). ācchedana = seizing back what was given.

hindi: जिससे स्वयं या दूसरे के द्वारा अत्यधिक धन वसूल किया गया हो; या जो अत्यधिक भार में लगाया गया हो; या जो दूसरे से सम्बन्ध तोड़कर आया हो;
english: one made to pay excessive money, either by oneself or through another; or one set to an excessive burden; or one that has come over after breaking with another;
notes: atyāhāritam artham: caused to bring (pay) wealth beyond measure; artham is an accusative of the thing exacted. bhaṅktvā param upasthitam: literally 'having broken (with) another, come (to him)'; it could also mean 'approached after (the king) broke faith with another'.

hindi: जो उपेक्षित किया गया हो, या असमर्थता से; जो याचना करने के बाद विरोध किया गया हो — ऐसा मित्र कठिनाई से वश में आता है और वश में आकर भी शीघ्र ही विरक्त हो जाता है।
english: one neglected, or through incapacity; one antagonised after having been solicited — such an ally is won over with difficulty and, once won, quickly becomes disaffected.
notes: upekṣitam aśaktyā vā: neglected (deliberately), or neglected through incapacity. 27cd closes the list begun in 22.

words.gloss: to the extent of one's power

hindi: जिस मित्र ने प्रयास किया हो या जो सम्मान के योग्य हो, पर मोह से उसका सम्मान न किया गया हो; या जो सम्मानित तो किया गया हो पर योग्य रूप से नहीं; या जो यथाशक्ति रोका गया हो;
english: An ally that has made efforts, or is worthy of honour, but is not honoured through delusion; or honoured, but not suitably; or held back to the extent of one's power;
notes: 28-29 form one sentence, closed by 29cd 'is to be won over and, once won, stays'. śaktito nivāritam: 'prevented (from its object) as far as one could'; the reference of nivārita is not stated. mohān = mohāt with sandhi before m-.

words.gloss: frightened by injury to a friend
because of alliance with the enemy

hindi: या जो किसी मित्र को पहुँचाई गई हानि से डरा हुआ हो, या शत्रु के साथ मेल के कारण शंकित हो, या जिसे दूष्यों के द्वारा तोड़ा जाना हो — ऐसा मित्र वश में किया जा सकता है और वश में आकर स्थिर रहता है।
english: or one frightened by injury done to a friend, or made suspicious because of an alliance with the enemy, or one whom treasonable persons seek to split off — such an ally can be won over and, once won, stays.
notes: mitra-upaghāta: injury done (by the king) to some other ally, which frightens this one. ari-saṃhitāt: from the king's association with this ally's enemy. dūṣyair bhedituṃ (mitram): an ally being worked on by treasonable persons to split it off; the infinitive is loosely attached.

hindi: इसलिए वह मित्र को हानि पहुँचाने वाले इन दोषों को उत्पन्न न करे; अथवा यदि वे उत्पन्न हो गए हों तो दोषों को नष्ट करने वाले गुणों से उन्हें शान्त करे।
english: Therefore he should not give rise to these faults that injure an ally; or, if they have arisen, he should quiet them with merits that counteract the faults.
